One fix, to watchlists. **90 of IBKR's 108 Trading endpoints, plus the socket**, as in `v0.4.0-preview.5`.

```sh
dotnet add package IbkrDotNet.Extensions.DependencyInjection --prerelease
```

## A negative watchlist identifier is written, not refused

`WatchlistsClient.CreateAsync` refused any identifier that was not all digits before sending anything, with a message saying IBKR requires it ([#80](https://github.com/jerbersoft/ibkrdotnet/issues/80)). IBKR's reference does say so — "Must be a number, digits 0-9 only" — but IBKR gave some older lists negative identifiers, and a live gateway takes a write under one. On the paper username where this was measured, 3 of 15 lists had one, all three `readOnly: false`, and all three could be read and deleted through this library but never saved.

Measured by hand against a Client Portal Gateway: a list's own 15 rows written back under `-6062842538047152184` answered `200` and moved its hash, and the username still had 15 lists — the list was replaced in place, not duplicated. Adding a contract and then removing it round-tripped the same way, and the list ended identical to where it started.

`CreateAsync` now accepts a single leading minus. Anything else is still refused before it is sent, because what IBKR does with a letter is undocumented and nothing has measured it, and the message now states the library's rule instead of attributing it to IBKR. The request body the client now sends for a negative identifier is the one sent by hand above, and a test pins it; the round trip through `CreateAsync` itself has not yet been run against a live gateway.

The same measurement settles the other half of IBKR's rule. An identifier is documented as unique, and one already in use replaces that watchlist in place rather than being refused. The doc comments on `CreateAsync` say so now, as does the README's reference: check `GetAllAsync` for the identifier first unless replacing the list is the point.

## What this breaks

Nothing in the public API. An identifier with a leading minus now reaches IBKR where it used to throw `ArgumentException`; every other identifier the client refused, it still refuses.

## Nothing else changed

576 tests, five of them new: one pins the request sent for a negative identifier, and four more malformed identifiers — a bare minus, a doubled one, one in the middle and a leading plus — are refused before anything is sent.

## Why this is still a prerelease

For the reason `v0.4.0-preview.1` gave — the public API is still settling — and because [#60](https://github.com/jerbersoft/ibkrdotnet/issues/60) is still open. [#79](https://github.com/jerbersoft/ibkrdotnet/issues/79) is also open and not addressed here: every thirty seconds the socket sends a frame a Client Portal Gateway cannot read, which the gateway logs as a `NullPointerException` and IBKR answers with `Topic unknown 'null'`.

## Publishing

Pushed by [Trusted Publishing](https://learn.microsoft.com/nuget/nuget-org/trusted-publishing) over OIDC, as the previous six versions were; both packages are also attached to this release.
